notes: The first day climbs about 600 m to the Panekire Range. The bluff edge is open to wind.
You must book the huts and campsites before you go.
Te Urewera is the homeland of Tūhoe. Read the Te Urewera notices before you go.

waiharuru.name: Waiharuru Hut and Campsite
waiharuru.note: DOC hut and campsite. 13 tent sites. You must book before you go. Facilities: heating, mattresses, non-flush toilets. Boil the water before you drink it.

marauiti.name: Marauiti Hut
marauiti.note: DOC hut. You must book before you go. Facilities: heating, mattresses, non-flush toilets. Boil the water before you drink it. It is 150 m from the track line on this map.

start.name: Onepoto
start.note: Start of the track at the south end of the lake. A water taxi or shuttle can bring you here.

end.name: Hopuruahine Landing
end.note: End of the track at the north end of the lake. Arrange a water taxi or shuttle before you go.

pois.name: Korokoro Falls
pois.text: Waterfall with a drop of 22 m. The side track from the junction near Korokoro campsite takes about 1 hour there and back.

pois.name: Panekire Range high point
pois.text: The highest part of the track, about 1170 m. The bluffs have wide views of the lake.
